findings.issue_text: Pre-existing P2: In incidents.py:80-93, when monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR, previous_checkins is set to only the single current failed check-in, so create_incident_occurrence receives a one-element list and get_failure_reason renders e.g. 'A missed check-in was detected' for every subsequent failure, contradicting the actual incident history (e.g. incident started with '3 missed check-ins')

Pre-existing P3: In incident_occurrence.py:152-155, get_monitor_environment_context builds config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy() and conditionally mutates it, but returns the unmutated monitor_environment.monitor.config, so the schedule_type normalization never takes effect and the context ships the raw integer schedule_type

Pre-existing P3: In incident_occurrence.py:157-163, get_failure_reason's docstring example 'A failed check-in was detected' is unreachable since the singular branch only produces 'An error/missed/timeout check-in was detected'

Pre-existing P3 (confidence 50): In incidents.py:39-44, the threshold query filters date_added__lte with order_by('-date_added') and no secondary tie-break key (e.g. id), making the sliced window nondeterministic when multiple check-ins share a timestamp, potentially including duplicates or excluding the boundary check-in and causing spurious incident start/missed detection

P3 / confidence 50 — incidents.py:88-94: MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...]) followed by a loop issuing Kafka production per check-in is a mini N+1 (pre-existing; impact negligible since previous_checkins is at most one entry in ERROR branch and threshold-bounded in OK/ACTIVE branch)

P3 / confidence 50 — incident_occurrence.py:37: monitor_env.get_last_successful_checkin() issues an extra query per occurrence produced (pre-existing; runs only once per incident transition/re-occurrence, minor impact)
SimpleCheckIn moved to types.py without a re-export shim; external importers of the old mark_failed.py location will raise ImportError

Dead variable in get_monitor_environment_context: config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy() is mutated but never used, so Kafka occurrence contains raw schedule_type integer instead of its display string

P2 — Dead code / broken transform: in get_monitor_environment_context (incident_occurrence.py:159-170), config = monitor.config.copy() with schedule_type conversion is computed but never used; the function returns the raw monitor.config dict, so the numeric schedule_type enum leaks into the occurrence's monitor context

P2 — Coupling/cross-layer type leak: get_monitor_environment_context serializes the raw monitor config dict directly into a Kafka event payload (incident_occurrence.py:165), making internal model representation (schedule_type numeric value, checkin_margin, max_runtime) an implicit contract with issues/snuba consumers

P3 — Redundant, fragile re-derivation of monitor_env from the check-in in incident_occurrence.py:26-31 and incidents.py:14-18; caller should pass monitor_env explicitly since it has already resolved/validated the environment, and duplicated None handling can silently no-op occurrence creation if monitor_environment is unfetched
P3 — Copy-paste risk: identical SimpleCheckIn dict literal built in three places (incidents.py:21-27 and incidents.py:66-70); extract a helper to prevent drift if the TypedDict gains fields

P3 — Misleading docstring in get_failure_reason (incident_occurrence.py:124-131): example says 'A failed check-in was detected' but the singular map produces 'An error/missed/timeout check-in was detected'

Race condition in try_incident_threshold: monitor_env.status is read without lock/select_for_update/F-condition, so concurrent failing check-ins can both flip status to ERROR and emit duplicate occurrences to Kafka
Status update via save(update_fields=('status',)) is not conditional on the prior value, providing no optimistic-concurrency guard

Silent-pass bug: in the MonitorStatus.ERROR branch, if active_incident is None the occurrence is silently skipped while monitor_environment_failed is still sent and True is returned, hiding the failure with no log or metric

ERROR-branch occurrence loses context of prior failures: previous_checkins contains only the single new failed check-in, so failure_reason under-reports incident severity on every check-in after the first

No status filter on threshold query: check-in window query only filters date_added__lte and doesn't exclude duplicate/stale statuses, so date_added ties with order_by('-date_added') can nondeterministically flip the 'any OK in window' decision

Dead/misleading code in get_monitor_environment_context: config copy and schedule_type conversion are computed but unused; returned dict embeds raw monitor.config so schedule_type is the raw value rather than display form

goldens.comment: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing P2: In incidents.py:80-93, when monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR, previous_checkins is set to only the single current failed check-in, so create_incident_occurrence receives a one-element list and get_failure_reason renders e.g. 'A missed check-in was detected' for every subsequent failure, contradicting the actual incident history (e.g. incident started with '3 missed check-ins')

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `incidents.py`), the `monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch sets `previous_checkins` to a single dict for the current `failed_checkin` (lines ~80-93 in the added file). That one-element list is passed to `create_incident_occurrence`, whose evidence calls `get_failure_reason(failed_checkins)`, which will indeed render the singular message for subsequent failures. However, the diff does not establish that the evidence is intended to summarize the entire incident history vs. the triggering check-in; so while the observation is grounded, calling it a definite correctness defect isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

matched_golden_ids: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the function creates/mutates a copied config (adding normalized/display values) but mistakenly returns the original monitor.config, so the modifications don’t take effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing P3: In incident_occurrence.py:157-163, get_failure_reason's docstring example 'A failed check-in was detected' is unreachable since the singular branch only produces 'An error/missed/timeout check-in was detected'

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows get_failure_reason()'s singular path always returns one of the strings in SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP ("An error...", "A missed...", "A timeout...") when sum(status_counts.values()) == 1. So the docstring example "A failed check-in was detected" is indeed not produced by this function as written. However, this is only a docstring/example mismatch and does not affect runtime behavior, making it a minor documentation/style nit rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pre-existing P3 (confidence 50): In incidents.py:39-44, the threshold query filters date_added__lte with order_by('-date_added') and no secondary tie-break key (e.g. id), making the sliced window nondeterministic when multiple check-ins share a timestamp, potentially including duplicates or excluding the boundary check-in and causing spurious incident start/missed detection

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py, the query used to build the threshold window orders only by "-date_added" and then slices (previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]). If multiple check-ins share the same date_added timestamp, SQL does not guarantee a deterministic order among ties without a secondary key (e.g., -id). That can make the chosen window nondeterministic at the boundary, potentially changing whether an OK check-in is included/excluded and thus whether an incident is triggered. This exact pattern is present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 / confidence 50 — incidents.py:88-94: MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...]) followed by a loop issuing Kafka production per check-in is a mini N+1 (pre-existing; impact negligible since previous_checkins is at most one entry in ERROR branch and threshold-bounded in OK/ACTIVE branch)

adjudication.rationale: In `incidents.py`, the code does `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...])` once and then iterates the resulting queryset to call `create_incident_occurrence` (Kafka production) per check-in. That is not an N+1 query pattern (there is a single DB query, not one query per check-in). While it does produce multiple Kafka messages when `previous_checkins` has multiple entries, that appears intentional and is threshold-bounded by `failure_issue_threshold`, so labeling it a “mini N+1” is a misread of what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 / confidence 50 — incident_occurrence.py:37: monitor_env.get_last_successful_checkin() issues an extra query per occurrence produced (pre-existing; runs only once per incident transition/re-occurrence, minor impact)
matched_golden_ids: The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point to an unnecessary extra database query when determining the last successful check-in. The golden specifies the redundancy comes from re-fetching MonitorCheckIn by ID even though prior check-in data is already available in previous_checkins; the candidate flags get_last_successful_checkin() as issuing an extra query in that same area, though it doesn’t explicitly mention previous_checkins as the already-available source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SimpleCheckIn moved to types.py without a re-export shim; external importers of the old mark_failed.py location will raise ImportError

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `SimpleCheckIn` `TypedDict` from `src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py` (it previously existed there) and adds it to `src/sentry/monitors/types.py`. There is no re-export/alias left behind in `mark_failed.py`, so any code that previously did `from sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed import SimpleCheckIn` would now fail with `ImportError`. The diff itself doesn’t show whether such importers exist, so this is a compatibility concern rather than a verifiable functional defect within the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead variable in get_monitor_environment_context: config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy() is mutated but never used, so Kafka occurrence contains raw schedule_type integer instead of its display string

adjudication.rationale: In `get_monitor_environment_context` (both the new `incident_occurrence.py` and the removed old version), `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` is conditionally mutated (`config["schedule_type"] = ...`) but the returned dict uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of `config`. This makes the `config` local effectively dead and means the produced Kafka occurrence context will not include the display string for `schedule_type` (it will keep the raw value from the model config).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Dead code / broken transform: in get_monitor_environment_context (incident_occurrence.py:159-170), config = monitor.config.copy() with schedule_type conversion is computed but never used; the function returns the raw monitor.config dict, so the numeric schedule_type enum leaks into the occurrence's monitor context

adjudication.rationale: In `get_monitor_environment_context` (new `incident_occurrence.py`), the code creates `config = monitor_environment.monitor.config.copy()` and conditionally replaces `config["schedule_type"]` with `get_schedule_type_display()`, but the returned dict uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the computed `config`. This makes the transform dead code and means any intended human-readable `schedule_type` value is not actually included in the occurrence context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Coupling/cross-layer type leak: get_monitor_environment_context serializes the raw monitor config dict directly into a Kafka event payload (incident_occurrence.py:165), making internal model representation (schedule_type numeric value, checkin_margin, max_runtime) an implicit contract with issues/snuba consumers

adjudication.rationale: In `create_incident_occurrence`, `event_data` includes `"contexts": {"monitor": get_monitor_environment_context(monitor_env)}`. `get_monitor_environment_context` returns `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`, which is the raw model config dict (it even creates a `config = ...copy()` and conditionally rewrites `schedule_type`, but then does not use `config` in the returned payload). This does expose internal config representation in the Kafka event payload and can create an implicit contract with downstream consumers, matching the finding. This is an architecture/coupling concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Redundant, fragile re-derivation of monitor_env from the check-in in incident_occurrence.py:26-31 and incidents.py:14-18; caller should pass monitor_env explicitly since it has already resolved/validated the environment, and duplicated None handling can silently no-op occurrence creation if monitor_environment is unfetched

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated resolution/guarding of `monitor_env` from `failed_checkin.monitor_environment` in both `try_incident_threshold` (incidents.py) and `create_incident_occurrence` (incident_occurrence.py). This is redundant and can be simplified by passing `monitor_env` explicitly to avoid repeated lookups/guards. However, the claim that an “unfetched” `monitor_environment` could cause `create_incident_occurrence` to silently no-op is not verifiable from the diff: Django will lazily fetch the related object when accessed, and the checkin IDs used come from a query constrained by `monitor_environment=monitor_env` (or the already-validated `failed_checkin`). So it’s more of a robustness/architecture concern than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Copy-paste risk: identical SimpleCheckIn dict literal built in three places (incidents.py:21-27 and incidents.py:66-70); extract a helper to prevent drift if the TypedDict gains fields

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same `SimpleCheckIn` dict literal constructed twice in `incidents.py` (once when `failure_issue_threshold == 1`, and once in the `MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch), not “three places”. The suggestion to extract a helper is a minor maintainability/style refactor and not an actionable, diff-specific review issue at the stated severity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Misleading docstring in get_failure_reason (incident_occurrence.py:124-131): example says 'A failed check-in was detected' but the singular map produces 'An error/missed/timeout check-in was detected'

adjudication.rationale: The finding is factually grounded (the docstring example includes "A failed check-in was detected" while the singular branch returns one of SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP messages like "An error check-in was detected"). However, this is only a docstring/example mismatch and does not indicate a functional defect or substantive review issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition in try_incident_threshold: monitor_env.status is read without lock/select_for_update/F-condition, so concurrent failing check-ins can both flip status to ERROR and emit duplicate occurrences to Kafka

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `incidents.py`), the code branches based on `monitor_env.status` without any transaction/locking (`select_for_update`) and then sets `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and emits occurrences via `create_incident_occurrence`. Two concurrent failing check-ins can both observe status `OK/ACTIVE`, both transition to `ERROR`, and both run the Kafka emission loop, producing duplicate occurrences. `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)` may prevent duplicate incident rows, but it does not prevent duplicate occurrence production in this race window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Status update via save(update_fields=('status',)) is not conditional on the prior value, providing no optimistic-concurrency guard

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the code sets `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and calls `monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",))` after checking `if monitor_env.status in [MonitorStatus.OK, MonitorStatus.ACTIVE]:`. However, this is not an optimistic-concurrency/atomic guard at the database level (no `UPDATE ... WHERE status IN (...)`, no `select_for_update`, no version check), so concurrent updates could overwrite a newer status. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness concern, but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent-pass bug: in the MonitorStatus.ERROR branch, if active_incident is None the occurrence is silently skipped while monitor_environment_failed is still sent and True is returned, hiding the failure with no log or metric

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), when `monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR` it sets `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` and proceeds. If `active_incident` is `None`, the guarded block `if not monitor_env.monitor.is_muted and not monitor_env.is_muted and incident:` skips creating any occurrence, yet `monitor_environment_failed.send(...)` is still executed and the function returns `True`. This matches the finding: the code path silently omits the occurrence while signaling failure and reporting success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ERROR-branch occurrence loses context of prior failures: previous_checkins contains only the single new failed check-in, so failure_reason under-reports incident severity on every check-in after the first

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold`, when `monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR`, `previous_checkins` is explicitly set to only the current `failed_checkin` (single-element list). That list is passed into `create_incident_occurrence`, and `get_failure_reason(failed_checkins)` will therefore describe only that single status rather than aggregating prior consecutive failures during the ongoing incident. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior, but whether it is a correctness defect is not verifiable from the diff alone (it may be intended to describe the triggering check-in only).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No status filter on threshold query: check-in window query only filters date_added__lte and doesn't exclude duplicate/stale statuses, so date_added ties with order_by('-date_added') can nondeterministically flip the 'any OK in window' decision

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the threshold window is built via `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(..., date_added__lte=failed_checkin.date_added).order_by("-date_added")...` and then sliced `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]`. Because ordering is only by `-date_added`, rows with identical `date_added` have undefined relative order, so the slice can include/exclude an `OK` check-in nondeterministically, which can flip the `any(checkin["status"] == OK ...)` decision and incident creation. A stable secondary ordering (e.g., `-date_added, -id`) would be needed to make the threshold window deterministic. The "no status filter" part is less substantiated, but the nondeterminism claim is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/misleading code in get_monitor_environment_context: config copy and schedule_type conversion are computed but unused; returned dict embeds raw monitor.config so schedule_type is the raw value rather than display form

adjudication.rationale: In `get_monitor_environment_context` (new in `incident_occurrence.py`), a copy of `monitor_environment.monitor.config` is made and `schedule_type` is converted to `get_schedule_type_display()`, but the returned dict uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified `config` variable. This makes the conversion dead code and causes the context to include the raw `schedule_type` value rather than the intended display value.
